newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lyonnaise H1 profit seen around 700 mln Fr.
newsitem.headline: Lyonnaise H1 profit seen around 700 mln Fr.

text.p: Analysts expect French utilities company Lyonnaise des Eaux to post first-half net attributable profit of around 700-730 million francs when it reports on Thursday, compared to a 506 million profit a year ago.

Analyst Dominique Carrel at broker CDC Bourse expects a first-half result in line with a full-year profit of around 1.3 billion francs, taking into account weakness in the building sector and poor performance of its GTM Entrepose unit.
But she said there would be an "absence of growth in cashflow", which would weaken Lyonnaise's balance sheet.

Carrel said GTM had cashflow of 257 million at the first half, down sharply from 704 million a year ago, while cashflow at another Lyonnaise unit, energy and heating specialist Elyo, only grew three percent at half time.
A second analyst at a leading Paris brokerage said he had pencilled in 700 million francs for interim profit and 1.3 billion francs, down from an initial 1.4 billion, for full year.
A third broker said he expected 730 million for the interim figure and 1.3 billion for the full year. The revision included poor construction results as shown in GTM's results and outlook.
The contruction and road-building sectors continue to drag on results and the group could incur restructuring costs, analysts said.
Lyonnaise owns 48 percent of GTM, which issued a profit warning on Tuesday and prompted brokers to downgrade forecasts for GTM to breakeven or a small loss from a profit.
Lyonnaise chairman Jerome Monod told an investment conference on September 6 he expected a profit rebound in first- half results and perhaps for the full year, but gave no figures.
The group recorded first half sales of 44.47 billion, versus 43.95 billion a year ago. It posted 1995 net attributable profit of 906 million francs, down from 1.06 billion in 1994.

The first half of the year is traditonally weak due to poor performance in the construction division, which is hit by winter weather, but there was scope for an improvement in the second half, the second analyst said.
The first half results could include a gain of some 250 million francs from Northumbrian Water Plc, which Lyonnaise acquired last year.

There should be few exceptional items in the period. Lyonnaise had 510 million francs in exceptional gains in 1995, most of which was booked in the second half with the sale of its funerals businesses.
Lyonnaise is currently trading at a discount to rival Cie General des Eaux.
One analyst put this down to the market's appreciation of the clear strategy set out by Generale des Eaux head Jean-Marie Messier, who talks a "language that the market appreciates."
Generale des Eaux has ambitions to be a major player in the telecommunications and media markets, areas which Messier expects to account for 40 percent of group sales by 2003.

In contrast, Lyonnaise is a classical utilities company, and a niche market player in television with its Metropole Television M6, which has a small market share of 14 percent, and its Paris Premiere cable channel.
Carrel said Lyonnaise's growth came from water, waste disposal and international operations and diversification such as GTM's offshore business.
Lyonnaise closed down 2.3 francs at 468, while Generale des Eaux ended up three at 531. The market was up 0.7 percent.
